svg.title: A merge request that only changes deployment files does not wait for the test suite: GitLab creates only the checks needed for a deployment-only merge request
svg.text: A merge request that only changes deployment files does
not wait for the test suite
Scenario: GitLab creates only the checks needed for a deployment-only merge request
Any other change keeps the whole pipeline

g.text: Given a project whose pipeline names a deployment folder and a single deployment file
The dotenv file names a folder and one file. A stored project variable lets GitLab decide before starting a runner,
without YAML list/source variables.
Then GitLab creates only code checks and release for the deployment-only merge request
This is the real GitLab pipeline for an image-tag change. The code checks and release remain; plan, build, test, deploy,
operate, monitor and feedback were never created. No runner is registered in this fixture: the cards prove job
selection, not job execution.
Then adding application code to the merge request restores the whole pipeline
The same merge request now changes application code too. GitLab creates all the jobs again, including code:lizard and
no-cheat.
Then build test and deploy actually execute when the stored policy keeps the full pipeline
These fixture tasks print execution markers. The shipped build/test/deploy scripts must actually invoke them when the
stored fallback keeps all jobs, despite a nonempty local deployment list.
Then a failed synchronization keeps the previous policy until a later plan repairs it
A failed plan leaves the previous selection active. Repair updates the project variable for new pipelines;
already-created job graphs stay unchanged.
Then the effective deployment setting can be previewed without editing the pipeline
Task reads dotenv precedence and prints the pattern. Empty, unsupported or overlong lists preserve every job; the
preview never writes YAML.
When a merge request contains a malformed deployment file
The deployment file contains an unfinished YAML list. This is the only file changed by the merge request.
Then MegaLinter checks only the changed deployment file
The project now gives only code:megalinter a runner. Its real log lists one changed file; unchanged application code is
not scanned.
Then MegaLinter rejects the malformed deployment YAML
The YAML validator names the deployment file and its syntax error. The job fails: checking fewer files still rejects
invalid deployment configuration.
Then fixing only the deployment YAML passes without scanning unchanged Python
Fixing the changed YAML passes despite the unchanged broken Python file. The same job log now shows successful YAML
validation.
Then a mixed Python change restores its syntax check
A mixed MR brings the Python file back into the full scan and reports its syntax error.
Then the reduced security scan rejects a privileged container
Checkov reports "Container should not be privileged" for the changed Pod. Its SARIF report identifies CKV_K8S_16 and the
deployment file.
Then correcting the privileged container passes the reduced security scan
Changing privileged to false removes the finding and the whole reduced security job succeeds. The same scanner policies
remain enabled.

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 13 steps · 13 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
● Given: stage ● When: actions ● Then: proofs
